topic: Observable PT-All design-quotient efficiency beyond chained DiD GMM. For fixed-T staggered adoption with declared cohort-specific structural observation-pattern supports, conditional pattern independence from the full potential-outcome path, no anticipation, overlap, finite fourth moments, and conditional PT-All, index every observable untreated cohort-time mean once and build its cohort-level/common-time design matrix A. Prove that null(A') is the complete observable linear PT-All restriction space; embed Bellégo's all-supported-link optimal-GMM restriction span L_B, compute the quotient Q=null(A')/L_B by rank-revealing elimination, and prove Q changes a target's efficiency bound iff its covariance-weighted target residual is nonzero. Derive the canonical gradient, exact Schur-complement gain, attaining cross-fitted one-step estimator, multiplier bands, and equality specialization to Bellégo. Include the seven-cell G3/G4/G5/never rotating-panel witness with patterns {1,3},{1,2},{2,3},{1,3}, unique quotient restriction, and n-scaled ATT variance improvement 16 to 40/3; audit Uhlemann's CBS rotating-firm chained-DiD application. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: With observable cells ordered as (G3,1),(G4,1),(G4,2),(G5,2),(G5,3),(never,1),(never,3), the presolver constructed the normalized six-column cohort/time design, proved rank(A)=6, and obtained the unique restriction vector (0,1,-1,1,-1,-1,1). Bellégo contributes no overidentifying row on this witness, so the quotient has rank one. With marginal-score covariance 4I, the direct ATT variance is 16, the restriction variance is 24, and target-restriction covariance is -8, yielding 16-64/24=40/3. Checks covered disconnected supports, separately sampled marginals, one-wave telescopes, singular covariance, target paths, Bellégo's all-k links, the Uhlemann sampling description, and adjacent literature without finding a collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the observed-data tangent-space factorization for arbitrary nonmonotone structural patterns with conditional covariates, showing that the efficient marginal-score vector followed by quotient projection is the full canonical gradient rather than only the best linear-GMM score. EARLY KILL TEST: Construct Bellégo's complete equations 23-24 moment matrix for the seven-cell witness, row-reduce it jointly with A, and stop if Bellégo already spans the quotient or if the constrained Gaussian Fisher bound differs from 40/3.

open_problems.open_problem: For fixed-T staggered adoption with arbitrary declared observation-pattern supports, characterize every observable linear implication of conditional PT-All and determine exactly which restrictions are absent from Bellégo, Benatia, and Dortet-Bernadet's all-supported-link GMM system.

source_refs.claim: The general-pattern analysis stacks supported k-period ATT increments through a link matrix and combines them by optimal GMM, while noting testable trend equalities across subpanels.
source_refs.author: Christophe Bellégo, David Benatia, Vincent Dortet-Bernadet

source_refs.claim: Design-matrix rank conditions separate identifying assumptions from targets and deliver an efficient linear estimator in a conventional observed staggered panel, not arbitrary structural patterns.
source_refs.author: Kirill Borusyak, Xavier Jaravel, Jann Spiess

source_refs.excerpt: unbalanced panels and estimated data-adaptive weights are left for a separate frontier
Define E_m and Z_m entrywise ... then recompute C without treating the selectors as black-box primitives.
Replace the tautological iff with an independent frontier characterization ... not just C := L_m - L_EIF.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bellégo et al. establish identification and optimal weighting for a chosen stack of supported within-unit links, but do not prove that those links exhaust all observable implications of PT-All. The web scan found no null-space completeness or quotient theorem for arbitrary nonmonotone supports. Independently, prior CausalSmith reviewers rejected related BJS efficiency quotients because their loading and selector matrices were asserted and their equality frontier unfolded a defined contrast. The first proof step must therefore construct both the cohort/common-time design A and Bellégo equations 23–24 entrywise, prove L_B is contained in null(A'), and row-reduce the two spaces independently before invoking covariance geometry.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem proving null(A') is the complete observable linear PT-All restriction space, giving a rank-revealing basis for null(A')/L_B, and showing by an exact Schur complement that the quotient lowers a specified ATT variance exactly when its covariance-weighted target residual is nonzero.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from unavailable long differences, through overlapping incomplete panels, to a concrete GMM system and rotating-panel payoff; then isolate the restrictions its links do not span.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Long-run effects require longitudinal contrasts -> rotating panels destroy many long differences -> supported short links recover some information -> ask whether PT-All supplies efficiency-relevant restrictions beyond every supported link

method_exemplars.technique: Stack all supported k-period cohort-time increments, encode their telescoping relations by the integer link matrix, and combine the overidentified system by covariance-weighted GMM.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its moment matrix is the donor construction whose row span becomes L_B; the resolution must preserve it while proving what lies outside it.

method_exemplars.technique: Use rank conditions on the untreated design, partial out nuisance components, and characterize the target-specific efficient linear estimator and its variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The quotient is likewise a design-matrix projection problem in which estimability and variance depend on the nuisance cohort/common-time column space.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive efficient staggered-DiD scores from overidentifying restrictions and implement feasible covariance-optimal, cross-fitted estimation with influence-function inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest full efficiency-and-attainment machinery once the new observation-pattern quotient has been identified.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive the full observed-data canonical gradient and semiparametric efficiency bound for conditional staggered-adoption ATT targets under PT-All with arbitrary nonmonotone structural observation patterns.

source_refs.claim: Optimal GMM combines the paper's selected link moments, but efficiency losses from propensity-score first steps under selection on observables are left to future work.
source_refs.author: Christophe Bellégo, David Benatia, Vincent Dortet-Bernadet

source_refs.claim: Efficient observed-data influence functions are derived for ATT with missing pre- or post-treatment outcomes in a two-period DiD model, not fixed-T staggered structural patterns.
source_refs.author: Lorenzo Testa, Edward H. Kennedy, Matthew Reimherr

source_refs.claim: For correlated outcomes missing at random, ordinary optimal GEE is generally inefficient relative to the full observed-data semiparametric bound.
source_refs.author: James M. Robins, Andrea Rotnitzky
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Under MAR, an augmented moment system can exhaust the extra conditional restrictions and represent the semiparametric efficiency bound.
source_refs.author: Bryan S. Graham

source_refs.excerpt: It is not the semiparametric efficiency bound for the full conditional-moment DDD model.
Derive the conditional-moment semiparametric efficient influence function for staggered DDD.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Optimal weighting of Bellégo's finite link stack establishes efficiency only within that chosen span; Robins and Rotnitzky show that this distinction can be strict in an analogous multivariate-missingness model. Testa, Kennedy, and Reimherr stop at a two-period missing-outcome DiD model, while Graham's augmented-moment equivalence does not incorporate staggered cohort-time PT-All restrictions or support-specific quotients. The same proof boundary appears in the banked DDD proposal, which explicitly disclaims the full conditional-moment bound. The missing first step is a factorization of every observed-data score by pattern, cohort, and covariates, including perturbations of the covariate law, pattern propensity, and each observed outcome margin, followed by the adjoint projection onto the PT-All restriction tangent.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An observed-data tangent-space decomposition for arbitrary nonmonotone supports, an explicit quotient-projected canonical gradient representing every ATT pathwise derivative, and a proof that its variance is the Hájek-Le Cam bound, including disconnected supports and singular marginal-score covariance.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its direct arc from a practically important missing-outcome DiD failure to observed-data influence functions, efficiency bounds, and attaining estimators, with staggered structural patterns as the destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: DiD efficiency theory usually assumes complete outcomes -> missingness changes the observed tangent space -> two-period MAR admits an explicit efficient influence function -> derive the corresponding gradient for fixed-T staggered PT-All with arbitrary patterns

method_exemplars.technique: Represent the observed-data nuisance tangent space under MAR, identify its orthogonal complement, and derive the optimal influence function for restrictions on correlated outcome vectors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A fixed-T potential-outcome path is a correlated vector observed through nonmonotone patterns; the new gradient solves the same projection problem with PT-All restrictions.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert a missing-data semiparametric bound into an augmented unconditional-moment problem using a conditional moment that exhausts remaining MAR information.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The claim that efficient marginal scores plus quotient projection exhaust all information is the analogous efficiency-equivalence statement for structured patterns.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute the canonical gradient under overidentified staggered-DiD restrictions and construct an efficient feasible estimator using conditional covariance weighting.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the closest staggered-DiD canonical-gradient projection, to be extended by observation-pattern tangent directions.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a cross-fitted one-step estimator and simultaneous multiplier bands that attain the PT-All quotient efficiency bound with conditional covariates, estimated nuisance functions, and possibly singular restriction covariance.

source_refs.claim: The paper carries parametric propensity-score first-step influence through a multiplier bootstrap and leaves correction of associated efficiency losses to future work.
source_refs.author: Christophe Bellégo, David Benatia, Vincent Dortet-Bernadet

source_refs.claim: Conditional staggered DiD admits influence-function asymptotics and multiplier-bootstrap simultaneous inference for group-time effects.
source_refs.author: Brantly Callaway, Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna

source_refs.claim: Neyman-orthogonal DiD scores permit machine-learning first steps and root-n inference in high-dimensional covariate settings.
source_refs.author: Neng-Chieh Chang

source_refs.claim: Doubly robust DiD estimators can attain the two-period semiparametric efficiency bound, with first-step effects entering valid inference.
source_refs.author: Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna, Jun B. Zhao

open_problems.why_unsolved: Callaway and Sant'Anna supply simultaneous inference for ordinary staggered group-time ATT, Chang and Sant'Anna-Zhao supply orthogonal or doubly robust DiD scores, and Bellégo supplies a multiplier bootstrap for its parametric link-GMM scores. None treats an estimated PT-All quotient whose basis is obtained by rank-revealing elimination, whose restriction covariance may be singular, and whose marginal scores use pattern-specific nuisance learners. The first changed proof step is joint Neyman orthogonality with respect to conditional means, pattern propensities, and the covariance-weighted quotient projection, so basis estimation and generalized-inverse perturbations vanish from the first-order expansion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An estimator theorem giving a cross-fitted asymptotically linear expansion with the quotient canonical gradient under explicit product-rate conditions, attainment of its efficiency bound, and uniform coverage of target and event-time contrasts by a studentized multiplier band valid under fixed-rank singular covariance.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its practical framing that flexible nuisance fitting can destroy root-n DiD inference, followed by an orthogonal-score construction and usable limit theory; the new obstacle is quotient estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Conditional DiD needs nuisance functions -> flexible learners create first-order bias -> orthogonal scores plus sample splitting restore inference -> make quotient-efficient estimation and simultaneous bands valid under structural patterns

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a Neyman-orthogonal score, cross-fit nuisance learners, and bound the remainder by products of nuisance errors to obtain root-n normality without Donsker assumptions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the quotient canonical gradient is known, it is the score to cross-fit; the new work proves that orthogonality survives the pattern and projection layers.

method_exemplars.technique: Stack group-time influence functions and use common observation-level multipliers to approximate the supremum distribution for simultaneous confidence bands.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired bands concern the same staggered ATT/event-time family, but replace ordinary group-time scores with quotient-efficient scores.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian comparison, anti-concentration, and conditional multiplier approximation for maxima of sums of influence-function vectors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the proof machinery for uniform bands after establishing the stacked quotient-efficient linear representation and covariance-rank conditions.

open_problems.open_problem: For the CBS rotating-firm design used by Uhlemann, determine whether survey-weighted chained DiD and the additional PT-All quotient restrictions identify the intended firm ATT under the actual stratified rotation and imputation protocol.

source_refs.claim: Annual resampling of small firms creates a CBS rotating panel; the application uses sampling weights, assumes sampling independence, and imputes missing observations from remaining firm outcomes.
source_refs.author: Jan-Philip R. Uhlemann

source_refs.claim: Incomplete-panel mixture expectations can differ from population expectations, requiring explicit reweighting and pattern-specific sampling independence.
source_refs.author: Christophe Bellégo, David Benatia, Vincent Dortet-Bernadet

source_refs.claim: In missing-data GMM the sampling probability need not be ancillary, and conditional-expectation projection can improve on inverse-probability weighting.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen, Han Hong, Alessandro Tarozzi

open_problems.why_unsolved: Uhlemann's application motivates structural pattern supports, but its published description moves from annual stratified resampling and survey weights to sampling independence and an imputation using a firm's remaining observations. Bellégo's theory warns that incomplete-panel mixture means need not equal population means and handles stratified reweighting separately; Chen, Hong, and Tarozzi show that sampling probabilities can change the efficiency bound. No located result maps the CBS size-stratified rotation, administrative linkage, and imputation protocol into the required conditional pattern-independence law. The first proof step is to write the inclusion and retention mechanism conditional on declared survey strata and adoption cohort, rather than assuming an iid incomplete-panel mixture.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A survey-design identification theorem giving sufficient and falsifiable conditions under which weighted observed cohort-time means identify the firm-population ATT, its quotient-efficient influence function and variance, and an audit that either verifies those conditions for CBS or gives a regime-specific counterexample.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its concrete automation-through-a-rotating-CBS-sample motivation and explicit sampling and imputation claims as the applied problem statement, without implying that it proposed the quotient method.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Firm automation has dynamic effects -> CBS resamples smaller firms and produces incomplete histories -> chained DiD retains many firms -> determine whether the actual survey design validates the target and leaves exploitable PT-All restrictions

method_exemplars.technique: Condition link identification on pair-specific sampling indicators, distinguish mixture from population expectations, and reweight for selection on observables before stacking moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uhlemann implements this method, so its assumptions are the exact correspondence conditions the CBS design audit must verify or refute.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive bounds for moment-defined parameters with incomplete primary data and auxiliary information, comparing conditional projection with IPW under known and unknown sampling probabilities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: CBS weights and linked outcomes pose the same question of whether sampling probabilities are ancillary and how auxiliary observations enter an efficient score.

method_exemplars.technique: Augment inverse-probability moments by conditional restrictions that exhaust information supplied by missing-at-random sampling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The PT-All quotient is intended to capture additional observable information beyond weighted chain moments, making augmented-moment equivalence the closest template.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one obtain uniformly valid inference for the PT-All quotient efficiency gain when the gain is zero, the quotient rank changes, or the target is locally orthogonal to the quotient?

source_refs.excerpt: no convergence rate, test, confidence interval, or full semiparametric-efficiency claim is made.
Add a practical diagnostic ... a consistent test or confidence interval for the estimated ... loss functional.
add a separate theorem giving consistent rank selection and variance-gap estimation.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked DDD result establishes only consistency of a descriptive quadratic efficiency-loss diagnostic, and an earlier BJS review separately requested consistent rank selection. At zero gain the loss functional has a vanishing first derivative; near a rank change, the estimated quotient basis and pseudoinverse are nonsmooth. Ordinary delta-method Wald inference therefore need not be uniform. The first proof step is a local asymptotic expansion that jointly tracks weak singular values, local target orthogonality, and nuisance-estimated covariance rather than fixing the quotient rank and differentiating a smooth quadratic.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local limit experiment for the estimated Schur-complement gain together with a uniformly size-controlled test and confidence set, based on directional or rank-adaptive bootstrap, and a stated local-power function against n-dependent nonzero quotient gains.

writing_exemplar.why: Its estimator-comparison framing makes precision losses operational for applied event-study choices; the new question is whether an estimated gain is statistically distinguishable from zero.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Robust estimators target the same ATT -> their use of untreated information changes precision -> a quotient predicts a nonnegative gain -> practitioners need uniformly valid evidence that the gain is nonzero

method_exemplars.technique: Use directional differentiability and a derivative-aware bootstrap for nonsmooth plug-in functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Rank selection, pseudoinversion, and a quadratic gain at its zero boundary create the nonregular plug-in geometry requiring directional inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian approximation and multiplier bootstrap with covariance and anti-concentration control for maxima of many statistics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies simultaneous calibration when gain diagnostics are reported over many ATT targets or event times.

literature_map:
Bellégo, Benatia, and Dortet-Bernadet (2025, JoE, arXiv:2301.01085) is the direct anchor: supported k-period ATT links are stacked through a link matrix and optimally combined by GMM under general missing patterns.
Bellégo et al. note testable cross-subpanel trend equalities but do not claim that their supported links exhaust every observable PT-All restriction.
They also leave correction of first-step propensity-estimation efficiency losses under selection on observables to future work.
Uhlemann (2026, Journal of Agricultural Economics, DOI 10.1111/1477-9552.70067) is the live CBS application: annual resampling creates a rotating firm panel, with survey weights, imputation, and chained-DiD simultaneous bands.
Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021, JoE, arXiv:1803.09015) supply conditional staggered group-time ATT influence functions and multiplier simultaneous inference.
Marcus and Sant'Anna (2021, JAERE, arXiv:2009.01963) show that stronger parallel-trends assumptions change recovered parameters and precision, but do not study arbitrary structural patterns.
Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024, ReStud, arXiv:2108.12419) give design-matrix rank conditions and efficient imputation for conventional staggered panels, the closest linear-algebra template.
Harmon (2024 working paper) proves best-linear-unbiased properties for chained or stepwise DiD under persistence, which is not a full observed-data semiparametric bound.
Sant'Anna and Zhao (2020, JoE, arXiv:1812.01723), Chang (2020, Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1812.10846), and Zimmert (arXiv:1809.01643) give efficient or orthogonal conditional DiD scores without arbitrary pattern quotients.
Testa, Kennedy, and Reimherr (2025, arXiv:2509.25009) derive missing-outcome DiD canonical gradients for a two-period MAR setting, exposing the uncovered fixed-T staggered case.
Robins and Rotnitzky (1995, JASA) show that optimal GEE for multivariate missing outcomes can remain globally inefficient.
Graham (2011, Econometrica) and Chen, Hong, and Tarozzi (2008, AoS, arXiv:0705.0069) supply augmented-moment and conditional-projection efficiency machinery for missing data.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1608.00060) provide orthogonal cross-fitting, and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, AoS, arXiv:1212.6906) provide multiplier approximation for maxima.
The unoccupied intersection is an exhaustive observable PT-All restriction theorem, its quotient over all supported chained links, and a proof that quotient projection gives the full canonical gradient under arbitrary nonmonotone supports.
prior_proposal_map:
A bounded catalogue scan covered proposal cores, archived rejected angles, reviewer JSONs, bank READMEs, and available writeups under doc/research.
The closest source was downgraded qid stat_ddd_overid_efficiency/v1, whose core and writeup explicitly stop at constant retained-score-span GMM optimality.
Its reviews/angle1_v6.json supplied two high-yield strengthening paths: derive the full conditional-moment EIF and add inference for the efficiency-loss diagnostic.
Failed qid eid_bjs_efficient_event_study/v1 supplied an earlier quotient-row-space attempt and reserved unbalanced panels and adaptive weights for another frontier.
Its reviews/angle1_v1.json requested an observable diagnostic with consistent rank selection and variance-gap estimation.
Failed qid eid_bjs_if_contrast_frontier/v1 and all four archived rejected angles were inspected; the final diagnosis was that estimator selectors were asserted and the iff contrast was tautological.
Its reviews/angle4_v3.json gives the direct prescription to derive moment matrices entrywise and characterize the row-space frontier independently.
No mined proposal contained a completed arbitrary-pattern PT-All tangent-space or design-quotient theorem.
